title: The Role of Stress in Breast Cancer Incidence: Risk Factors, Interventions, and Directions for the Future
focus: non-genetic risk in young adult breast cancer

population_focus.notes: some effects (e.g., perceived stressful life events) appeared stronger in pre/perimenopausal women in cited studies

key_numbers: Striking life events OR 1.50 (95% CI 1.15–1.97); severe striking events OR 2.07 (95% CI 1.06–4.03)
Job strain meta-analysis: breast cancer HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.82–1.14) (null)
Black Women’s Health Study: discrimination (job) IRR 1.32 (95% CI 1.03–1.70); discrimination in job/housing/police IRR 1.48 (95% CI 1.01–2.16) in <50 yrs
CRP and breast cancer pooled OR 1.16 (95% CI 1.06–1.27); stronger in Asian samples OR 1.57 (95% CI 1.25–1.96)
Prospective high-risk cohort: acute stressors HR 1.03 (0.99–1.08), chronic stressors HR 1.00 (0.90–1.11) (null)
UK Breakthrough Generations (n≈106,612): no overall association for self-reported stress/adverse events

magnitude.per_unit: any history vs none; severity matters

population.age: all; stronger signals reported in pre/perimenopausal in some studies

factors.notes: Severity and timing (windows of susceptibility) matter; heterogeneity and misclassification across studies; publication bias considered in some reviews

factors.factor: perceived cumulative stress from major life events
factors.measurement: perceived stress linked to life events; cumulative indices
factors.notes: Dose–response reported; stronger effect pre/perimenopausal; needs replication with rigorous confounder control
No appreciable association with breast cancer risk across large cohorts

factors.measurement: retrospective/prospective ACE inventories; biomarkers (adiponectin, C-peptide, hsCRP, IGF-1)
factors.notes: Linked to toxic stress and to biomarkers associated with breast cancer; prospective links to incidence inconsistent; recall bias and under-measurement common

magnitude.per_unit: job discrimination; up to IRR 1.48 across job/housing/police; ER− OR 1.09 with Jim Crow birth cohort context

factors.measurement: self-reported major/everyday discrimination; historical structural exposure

population.age: effects strongest in <50 yrs in BWHS; race-specific analyses

factors.notes: Associated with higher inflammation (CRP, cytokines) and adverse health behaviors; structural racism context matters

factors.measurement: varied (PSS, life events, job strain); biological pathways via HPA/SAM, cortisol, inflammation
factors.notes: Overall incidence evidence equivocal; severity, chronicity, timing, coping, and social support likely moderate effects

factors.measurement: not quantified here; discussed as coping pathway
factors.notes: Stress/discrimination associated with higher alcohol consumption; alcohol is an established breast cancer risk factor

conclusion: Evidence linking stress to breast cancer incidence is mixed overall, but severe/striking life events and major discrimination show modest risk increases (particularly in younger women), while job strain appears null; better cumulative stress measurement, attention to timing, severity, coping, social support, and biologic pathways (inflammation/HPA) are needed to clarify risk in young/premenopausal women.

provenance.notes: Effect sizes extracted as reported; no tables used
